stem_tex: Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}(4x^2-4)/(x-1)&x\ne1\\4&x=1\end{cases}$. Which statements are true? I. $\lim_{x\to1}f(x)$ exists. II. $f$ is continuous at $1$. III. $f$ is differentiable at $1$.
explanation_tex: Away from $1$, $f(x)=4(x+1)$, whose limit is $8$. Since $f(1)=4$, the function is discontinuous and therefore not differentiable there. Only I holds.

stem_tex: Let $g(x)=\begin{cases}x^2&x\le3\\6x-9&x>3\end{cases}$. Which statements are true? I. $\lim_{x\to3}g(x)$ exists. II. $g$ is continuous at $3$. III. $g$ is differentiable at $3$.
explanation_tex: Both branches approach $9=g(3)$, proving continuity. The left derivative is $2(3)=6$, matching the right derivative $6$. All three statements hold.

stem_tex: Why does $f(x)=x^{2/3}$ on $[-8,8]$ fail the hypotheses of the Mean Value Theorem?
explanation_tex: The real cube root makes $f$ defined and continuous everywhere, but $f'(x)=\frac23x^{-1/3}$ for $x\ne0$. At zero the difference quotient has no finite limit, so differentiability on the open interval fails.

explanation_tex: Both endpoint values are zero, so the secant slope is zero. Solve $f'(x)=6x^2-6=0$ inside $(0,\sqrt3)$ to obtain $x=1$.

stem_tex: Let $f$ be twice continuously differentiable on $\mathbb R$. Suppose $[f(a+h)-f(a)]/h\ge f\prime(a)$ for every real $a$ and every $h>0$. Which statement must hold?
explanation_tex: For fixed $a$, Taylor expansion gives $[f(a+h)-f(a)]/h=f\prime(a)+\frac12 f\prime\prime(a)h+o(h)$. The assumed inequality, divided by positive $h$ and followed by $h\to0^+$, gives $f\prime\prime(a)\ge0$. Since $a$ is arbitrary, this holds everywhere.
